variants.title: TARGETED SKULL & CRANIAL TRAUMA ULTRASOUND REPORT

blocks.x: CLINICAL INDICATION:
[Mechanism of trauma, time post-injury, presenting signs, and exact anatomical site of swelling / impact]
Comparison: [Prior imaging / None available]
TECHNIQUE:

High-Resolution Scalp & Calvarial Survey performed using a high-frequency linear array transducer (12–18 MHz) with targeted interrogation of the site of impact and a complete survey of the cranial vault and suture lines.

Transcranial & Near-Field Evaluation performed via the anterior fontanelle, posterior fontanelle, and temporal acoustic windows using a micro-convex / sector transducer (5–9 MHz) and a linear probe for near-field extra-axial assessment.
Vascular Interrogation: Color and spectral Doppler evaluation of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries.
FINDINGS:
EXTRACRANIAL SOFT TISSUES & SCALP (Site of Impact: [Region]):
Subcutaneous Layer: [Normal thickness / Focal echogenic edema / Discrete hematoma measuring ___ x ___ x ___ cm].
Sub-aponeurotic (Subgaleal) Space: [Unremarkable / Fluid or blood collection crossing suture lines and midline].
Subperiosteal Space: [Normal / Lentiform biconvex collection strictly bounded by suture lines].
CALVARIAL BONE CORTEX & VAULT INTEGRITY:
Outer & Inner Table Cortex: [Smooth, continuous, uninterrupted echogenic cortical lines / Focal cortical discontinuity or step-off].
Fracture Evaluation: [No sonographic evidence of linear or depressed skull fracture / Focal cortical defect identified at ___].
Sutures & Fontanelles: [Normal anatomical alignment, width, and closure status of sagittal, coronal, lambdoid, and metopic sutures; no diastasis].
EXTRA-AXIAL SPACES (NEAR-FIELD & CONVEXITIES):
Epidural / Subdural Spaces: [Normal physiological extra-axial space width without abnormal echogenicity, fluid collection, or acute hematoma].
Subarachnoid Space: [Normal sulcal fluid width bilaterally].
BRAIN PARENCHYMA & MIDLINE STRUCTURES:
Cerebral Hemispheres: [Symmetric hemispheres with normal homogeneous parenchymal echogenicity; no focal hyperechoic cortical contusion, ischemic changes, or intraparenchymal hemorrhage].
Deep Gray Matter: [Normal echogenicity and symmetry of the basal ganglia and thalami].
Posterior Fossa: [Intact cerebellar hemispheres and vermis].
Ventricular System: [Lateral, third, and fourth ventricles are normal in size, caliber, and configuration, without compression, effacement, or intraventricular blood].
Midline Structures: [Septum pellucidum and third ventricle are central; zero midline shift].
CEREBRAL HEMODYNAMICS (DOPPLER):
Anterior / Middle Cerebral Arteries: [Normal antegrade systolic and diastolic flow velocities with normal Resistive Index (RI = 0.__, normal range 0.60–0.78)].
IMPRESSION / OPINION:
[Primary extracranial / skeletal finding, e.g., Intact calvarial bone cortex with no sonographic evidence of skull fracture.]
[Primary intracranial finding, e.g., Normal transcranial sonogram with no acute extra-axial hematoma, parenchymal contusion, or mass effect.]

[Clinical correlation & limitation: Ultrasound evaluation of the skull base, posterior fossa, and peripheral convexities is limited by acoustic bone shadowing; non-contrast head CT should be performed if clinical suspicion persists or neurological status deteriorates.]

variants.title: TARGETED SKULL & CRANIAL TRAUMA ULTRASOUND REPORT (NORMAL STUDY)

blocks.x: CLINICAL INDICATION:
[Mechanism of trauma, time post-injury, presenting signs, and site of clinical concern / swelling]
Comparison: [None available / Prior imaging]
TECHNIQUE:

High-Resolution Scalp & Calvarial Survey performed using a high-frequency linear array transducer (___ MHz) with targeted focus over the site of impact and systematic scanning of all major calvarial bones.

Transcranial & Near-Field Evaluation performed via the anterior fontanelle (patent / partially patent) and temporal acoustic windows using a micro-convex transducer (___ MHz) and a high-resolution linear probe for superficial extra-axial evaluation.
Vascular Interrogation: Color and spectral Doppler interrogation of the anterior cerebral artery.
FINDINGS:
EXTRACRANIAL SOFT TISSUES & SCALP (Site of Impact: [Region]):

Subcutaneous Layer: [Normal soft tissue thickness and echogenicity / Mild localized subcutaneous thickening and hyperechoic edema measuring ___ x ___ x ___ cm] over the site of clinical impact. There is no discrete fluid collection, subgaleal hemorrhage, or subperiosteal hematoma.
Sub-aponeurotic (Subgaleal) Space: Unremarkable. No fluid or blood collection crossing suture lines.
Subperiosteal Space: Normal architecture; no subperiosteal fluid or clot collection.
CALVARIAL BONE CORTEX & VAULT INTEGRITY:

Outer & Inner Table Cortex: The outer and inner table cortical margins of the [region] bone and adjacent calvarium demonstrate smooth, continuous, uninterrupted echogenic lines. There is no cortical step-off, focal interruption, or surface irregularity.
Fracture Evaluation: No sonographic evidence of a linear, depressed, or basilar skull fracture.
Sutures & Fontanelles: The coronal, sagittal, metopic, and lambdoid sutures demonstrate normal physiological width and sharp, well-corticated margins without diastasis or abnormal widening.
EXTRA-AXIAL SPACES (NEAR-FIELD & CONVEXITIES):

Epidural / Subdural Spaces: Near-field linear evaluation through the anterior fontanelle and high frontoparietal convexities reveals normal physiological extra-axial space width. No echogenic or anechoic extra-axial fluid collection, acute epidural hematoma, or subdural hematoma is identified.
Subarachnoid Space: Normal sulcal fluid width bilaterally.
BRAIN PARENCHYMA & MIDLINE STRUCTURES:

Cerebral Hemispheres: Both cerebral hemispheres are symmetric and demonstrate normal, age-appropriate sulcation and homogeneous parenchymal echogenicity. There is no focal hyperechoic cortical contusion, white matter injury, or intraparenchymal hemorrhage.
Deep Gray Matter: The basal ganglia and thalami show normal bilateral symmetry, contour, and baseline echogenicity.
Posterior Fossa: Visualized cerebellar hemispheres and vermis are structurally intact and unremarkable.

Ventricular System: The lateral ventricles (frontal horns and bodies), third ventricle, and fourth ventricle are normal in caliber, size, and symmetry. There is no ventricular dilatation, compression, effacement, or intraventricular echogenic blood debris.
Midline Structures: The septum pellucidum and third ventricle are strictly midline. There is zero midline shift or mass effect.
CEREBRAL HEMODYNAMICS (DOPPLER):

Anterior Cerebral Artery: Spectral Doppler interrogation demonstrates normal waveform morphology with brisk systolic upstroke and forward diastolic flow. Resistive Index (RI) is calculated at 0.__ (within normal physiological limits of 0.60–0.78), indicating normal cerebral perfusion pressures.
IMPRESSION / OPINION:
[Normal soft tissues of the scalp / Mild localized ___ subcutaneous soft tissue edema at the site of impact] without underlying subcutaneous, subgaleal, or subperiosteal hematoma.
Intact calvarial bone cortex with no sonographic evidence of a linear or depressed skull fracture.

Normal transcranial and near-field sonographic evaluation of the brain parenchyma, ventricular system, and extra-axial spaces, with no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, contusion, or mass effect.

Note: While ultrasound demonstrates high sensitivity for superficial soft tissue and calvarial injuries in accessible regions, definitive exclusion of occult skull base fractures, micro-contusions, or small extra-axial collections requires non-contrast head CT if clinical symptoms evolve.

bank_title: TRAUMA ULTRASOUND REPORTING PHRASES BANK (BY ANATOMICAL SECTION)

subs.title: Normal Scalp
items: Normal scalp soft tissue thickness and echogenicity over the site of clinical concern, with no focal fluid collection or hematoma.
Subcutaneous, sub-aponeurotic (subgaleal), and subperiosteal spaces are unremarkable.

subs.title: Subcutaneous Edema
items: Mild, localized subcutaneous soft tissue thickening and hyperechoic edema at the site of clinical impact, measuring ___ x ___ x ___ cm, without discrete fluid collection.
Increased subcutaneous echogenicity with loss of normal fat lobulation (cobblestone pattern), in keeping with soft tissue edema.

subs.title: Subcutaneous Hematoma
items: Discrete hypoechoic to heterogeneous collection within the subcutaneous fat measuring ___ x ___ x ___ cm, superficial to the galea aponeurotica, with no extension across suture lines.
No internal vascularity on Color Doppler.

subs.title: Caput Succedaneum (Neonates)
items: Diffuse, ill-defined scalp swelling with thickened echogenic subcutaneous tissue (___ cm), crossing suture lines and the midline, without a discrete organized collection.
No underlying subperiosteal collection or skull fracture.

subs.title: Subgaleal Hematoma
items: Large, heterogeneous, poorly marginated fluid / blood collection within the sub-aponeurotic (subgaleal) space measuring ___ x ___ cm, freely crossing the cranial suture lines and midline.
Internal echogenic debris with fluid-fluid level, in keeping with evolving blood products.
Large subgaleal collection: clinical correlation with hemodynamic status is advised (potential for significant blood loss in infants).

subs.title: Cephalohematoma (Subperiosteal Hematoma)
items: Well-defined, lentiform (biconvex) hypoechoic / heterogeneous subperiosteal collection over the [parietal / frontal / occipital] bone measuring ___ x ___ x ___ cm, strictly bounded by the adjacent suture margins and not crossing the midline.
Underlying calvarial cortex is intact / Underlying linear cortical defect identified (see Skull Cortex section).
Peripheral echogenic rim suggesting early calcification / ossification (subacute to chronic cephalohematoma).

subs.title: Organized / Chronic Hematoma
items: Relatively large, well-defined focal lesion showing heterogeneous, predominantly cystic appearance with multiple internal septations, low-level internal echoes, and turbid fluid content.
Peripheral vascular channels on Color Doppler, suggestive of an organized post-traumatic hematoma.

subs.title: Acute vs. Subacute Evolution
items: Acute: echogenic / isoechoic blood collection with internal mobile debris.
Subacute: evolving toward a hypoechoic / anechoic liquefied hematoma with internal fibrin strands and septations.

subs.title: Scalp Laceration / Foreign Body
items: Linear hypoechoic soft tissue defect through the subcutaneous layer at the site of laceration, with surrounding edema.
Echogenic focus within the scalp soft tissues with posterior acoustic shadowing and a surrounding hypoechoic rim, suspicious for a foreign body measuring ___ mm.

subs.title: Normal Cortex & Sutures
items: Smooth, continuous, uninterrupted echogenic outer and inner table cortical lines with no cortical step-off or surface irregularity.
No sonographic evidence of a linear, depressed, or basilar skull fracture.
Coronal, sagittal, metopic, and lambdoid sutures demonstrate normal physiological width and sharp, well-corticated margins without diastasis.

subs.title: Linear Skull Fracture
items: Sharp linear cortical discontinuity (___ mm gap) involving the [parietal / frontal / temporal / occipital] bone, without significant inward displacement, consistent with a non-displaced linear skull fracture.
Fracture margins are sharp and non-corticated; the defect does not communicate with the adjacent sutures.
Directly beneath the overlying [subperiosteal / subgaleal] hematoma.

subs.title: Depressed Skull Fracture
items: Focal inward buckling and distinct cortical step-off of the outer and inner calvarial tables spanning ___ x ___ cm, with maximal inward displacement of ___ mm relative to the adjacent intact cortex.
Inward displacement exceeds the thickness of the adjacent calvarium (___ mm).
Focal effacement of the subarachnoid space and flattening of the underlying gyral contour beneath the depressed segment.

subs.title: Ping-Pong / Greenstick Fracture
items: Smooth inward buckling of the calvarium without full-thickness cortical disruption, apex displaced ___ mm, with spring-like recoil on gentle transducer pressure.

subs.title: Comminuted / Stellate Fracture
items: Multiple radiating cortical discontinuities with bony fragmentation and step-off, centered on the [region] bone, with overlying soft tissue hematoma.

subs.title: Sutural Diastasis
items: Abnormal widening of the [coronal / sagittal / lambdoid] suture measuring ___ mm compared to the contralateral side, indicative of traumatic sutural diastasis.

subs.title: Fracture Mimics (Normal Suture / Vascular Groove)
items: Linear lucency follows the expected anatomical course of the ___ suture, with smooth, well-corticated margins and a symmetrical contralateral counterpart; no step-off or overlying hematoma. Normal suture, not a fracture.
Accessory suture (e.g., metopic suture / sutura mendosa) with corticated margins and bilateral symmetry; no associated soft tissue swelling.
Branching, tapering linear lucency with smooth corticated walls and low-velocity flow on Color / Power Doppler, consistent with a vascular groove / emissary channel rather than a fracture.

subs.title: Normal Extra-Axial Spaces
items: Normal physiological extra-axial space width. No echogenic or anechoic extra-axial fluid collection, acute epidural hematoma, or subdural hematoma identified.
Normal sulcal fluid width and subarachnoid space bilaterally.

subs.title: Epidural Hematoma (EDH)
items: Well-demarcated, biconvex (lentiform), homogeneously echogenic extra-axial mass along the [temporoparietal] convexity measuring ___ cm in length by ___ cm in maximal thickness.
Collection is bounded by suture attachments and displaces the echogenic dura mater and cerebral cortex medially.
Underlying linear skull fracture with overlying scalp hematoma (if present).
[Associated mass effect / No significant mass effect].

subs.title: Acute Subdural Hematoma (SDH)
items: Crescent-shaped (concavo-convex) echogenic extra-axial collection layering along the [right / left] cerebral convexity, crossing suture lines, measuring ___ cm in maximal thickness.
Effacement of adjacent cortical sulci with medial displacement of the cortex.
Interhemispheric (falcine) subdural collection with echogenic content, measuring ___ mm.

subs.title: Subacute / Chronic Subdural Collection
items: Crescentic extra-axial collection with mixed echogenicity, internal septations, and hypoechoic / anechoic liquefied components, measuring ___ cm in maximal thickness.

Bilateral / multifocal subdural collections of differing echogenicity in an infant: clinical correlation (including for possible non-accidental injury) and further imaging with CT / MRI are recommended.

subs.title: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage / Space Effacement
items: Increased echogenicity within the sulci and interhemispheric fissure, suspicious for subarachnoid blood.
Focal or diffuse effacement of the hemispheric sulci and subarachnoid fluid spaces beneath the site of impact.

subs.title: Technical Limitations
items: Acoustic shadowing from the [parietal / temporal] bone and overlying hematoma limits complete visualization of the subjacent epidural space beneath the fracture site.
Reverberation and shadowing artifacts from the angled bone limit deep cortical interface clarity.

subs.title: Normal Brain
items: Both cerebral hemispheres are symmetric with normal, age-appropriate sulcation and homogeneous parenchymal echogenicity. No focal hyperechoic contusion, white matter injury, or intraparenchymal hemorrhage.
Basal ganglia and thalami show normal bilateral symmetry, contour, and echogenicity.
Cerebellar hemispheres and vermis are structurally intact and unremarkable.
Lateral, third, and fourth ventricles are normal in size, caliber, and symmetry, without dilatation, compression, effacement, or intraventricular blood.
Septum pellucidum and third ventricle are strictly midline; zero midline shift or mass effect.

subs.title: Cortical Contusion
items: Focal ill-defined hyperechoic cortical / subcortical zone at the site of coup / contrecoup impact in the [region], suspicious for hemorrhagic parenchymal contusion.

subs.title: Intraparenchymal Hemorrhage
items: Well-defined echogenic intraparenchymal focus measuring ___ x ___ cm in the [lobe], with surrounding hypoechoic edema rim.

subs.title: Intraventricular Hemorrhage
items: Echogenic clot / layering debris within the [right / left] lateral ventricle, with ventricular dilatation measuring ___ mm.

subs.title: Cerebral Edema
items: Diffusely increased parenchymal echogenicity with loss of gray-white differentiation, effaced sulci, and slit-like ventricles, suggesting diffuse cerebral edema.

subs.title: Mass Effect & Midline Shift
items: Marked mass effect evidenced by effacement of the ipsilateral lateral ventricle, early entrapment / dilatation of the contralateral ventricle, and a ___ mm [rightward / leftward] shift of the septum pellucidum and third ventricle.
Compression and medial displacement of the [left / right] frontoparietal and temporal lobes.
Downward crowding at the tentorial incisura; fourth ventricle faintly visible and midline.

subs.title: Normal Doppler
items: Normal antegrade systolic and diastolic flow velocities with brisk systolic upstroke. Resistive Index (RI) = 0.__ (normal range 0.60–0.78), indicating normal cerebral perfusion pressures.

subs.title: Elevated Intracranial Pressure
items: Spectral Doppler demonstrates blunted, high-resistance diastolic flow with an elevated Resistive Index (RI = 0.__, normal < 0.78), indicating regional intracranial hypertension and compromised cerebral perfusion.
Absent or reversed end-diastolic flow, suggesting critically elevated intracranial pressure; urgent clinical correlation is required.

subs.title: Doppler of Collections / Skull Defects
items: Collection is avascular on Color Doppler, with no internal flow.
Peripheral vascularity within the septations on Color Doppler.

subs.title: Normal Study
items: Intact calvarial bone cortex with no sonographic evidence of skull fracture.
Normal transcranial and near-field sonographic evaluation with no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, contusion, or mass effect.

subs.title: Fracture / Hematoma
items: Non-depressed linear [region] skull fracture (___ mm cortical gap) underlying a [moderate-sized] subperiosteal hematoma (cephalohematoma).
Depressed [region] skull fracture with ___ mm of inward cortical displacement.
Large acute [region] epidural hematoma (___ cm maximal thickness) with ___ mm midline shift.

subs.title: Recommendations & Communication
items: Because acoustic shadowing from the calvarium can obscure a small underlying extra-axial bleed, non-contrast head CT is recommended to exclude an occult epidural hematoma.
Urgent: STAT non-contrast head CT and neurosurgical consultation are recommended.

Ultrasound evaluation of the skull base, posterior fossa, and peripheral convexities is limited by acoustic bone shadowing; CT is advised if clinical suspicion persists or neurological status deteriorates.
Findings were communicated directly to Dr. ______ at ______.
